name: Außervillgraten
kurzbeschreibung: Original alpine valley in the Villgratner Bergen – a paradise for hikers and those seeking tranquility.
beschreibung:
Overview

Außervillgraten is an authentic mountain village in the Lienz district of East Tyrol, nestled at approximately 1,287 meters above sea level at the entrance of the Villgraten Valley. Branching off from the Upper Puster Valley near Heinfels, the valley is considered one of the most unspoiled high-alpine valleys in the Eastern Alps. With around 750 residents, the municipality spans sunny mountain slopes and the secluded twelve-kilometer Winkeltal valley, culminating at Mount Hochgrabe at 2,951 meters, the highest peak of the Villgraten Mountains. Together with neighbouring Innervillgraten, Außervillgraten belongs to the prestigious network of Mountaineering Villages (Bergsteigerdörfer). The community has consciously eschewed mega-resorts and lift developments, instead captivating visitors with centuries-old timber farmhouses, pristine alpine pastures, and brilliant dark skies free from light pollution.

History

Human history in the valley spans over twelve centuries. In 769, Duke Tassilo III of Bavaria granted the uninhabited forested valley to Innichen Abbey for clearing and Christian mission. During the High Middle Ages, Bavarian settlers developed cattle-farming farmsteads (Schwaighöfe), which evolved into independent hereditary homesteads from the 15th century onwards. A celebrated cultural treasure is the heritage-listed Wurzerhof farm ensemble in Winkeltal, with roots dating back to 1433. The complex includes an ancient farmhouse, a traditional grain mill, a Venetian water-powered sawmill, a carpenter's workshop, and a private chapel. The parish church dedicated to Saint Gertrude of Nivelles was erected between 1795 and 1797 in a transition style from Late Baroque to Early Neoclassicism; its patron saint Gertrude is exceptionally rare throughout the Alpine realm.

How to Get There

By car, visitors reach Außervillgraten from Lienz or South Tyrol via the Drautal federal highway B100 to Heinfels/Panzendorf. From there, the well-constructed Villgratental road L325 leads six kilometers directly into the village center. Rail passengers use the Puster Valley Railway to Sillian railway station or the Heinfels stop. Regional VVT bus route 962 runs regularly between Sillian, Heinfels, and Außervillgraten throughout the valley.

Tips

An unforgettable outdoor excursion is a hike through the pristine Winkeltal valley along the tumbling mountain stream to the rustic Volkzeiner Hütte at 1,886 meters. Heritage lovers should visit the open-air Wurzerhof ensemble to discover authentic traditional rural craftsmanship. Experienced mountaineers can summit the 2,951-meter Hochgrabe for sweeping panoramas across the High Tauern and the Dolomites. Food lovers can indulge in homemade Villgrater Schlipfkrapfen and traditional Tirler barley soup in cozy village taverns. In winter, the valley transforms into a premier sanctuary for ski touring and snowshoeing far away from bustling ski circuits.
